title: Planning a Debate
text:
A debate outline is a plan that helps a speaker organize their arguments before a debate. Most outlines begin with a clear claim, which states the position the speaker will defend. After the claim, the speaker lists three main reasons and supports each reason with evidence, such as facts, examples, or expert opinions. Good outlines also anticipate the arguments of the other side.

Students often find that writing an outline makes them think more carefully about their topic. When they write the reasons on paper, they can see which points are weak and need more support. An outline also helps the speaker keep track of time during the debate. Many coaches recommend practicing the outline aloud before the real event.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what does a debate outline usually begin with?
options: A summary of the other side

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what does writing an outline help students see?
options: Which judge will vote for them
How long the audience will listen
Which points are weak and need more support

questions.text: What can be inferred about a speaker who writes an outline before a debate?
options: They probably plan to speak without any preparation
They probably want to be better prepared and organized
They probably do not care about the other side's arguments
They probably intend to avoid the debate

questions.text: Why would a coach recommend practicing the outline aloud?
options: To make the paper look more professional
To remove all the evidence from the speech
To check the timing and hear how the speech sounds
To memorize the other side's arguments

vocabulary.definition: a plan or summary of the main points of something
a statement of a position that someone will defend
facts, examples or opinions that support an argument
to expect something to happen and prepare for it in advance

paragraph_translations: Un esquema de debate es un plan que ayuda a un orador a organizar sus argumentos antes de un debate. La mayoría de los esquemas empiezan con una afirmación clara, que indica la postura que el orador defenderá. Después de la afirmación, el orador enumera tres razones principales y apoya cada razón con pruebas, como datos, ejemplos u opiniones de expertos. Los buenos esquemas también anticipan los argumentos del otro lado.

Muchos estudiantes descubren que escribir un esquema les hace pensar con más cuidado sobre su tema. Cuando escriben las razones en papel, pueden ver qué puntos son débiles y necesitan más apoyo. Un esquema también ayuda al orador a controlar el tiempo durante el debate. Muchos entrenadores recomiendan practicar el esquema en voz alta antes del evento real.
